text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- AEX index of Dutch blue chips adds 7.88 points to close just off record intraday high at 669.55. (p1)
- Former shareholders in bankrupt charter airline Air Holland take ABN Amro bank to court, charging the bank's prospectus for the 1989 bourse launch was misleading. (p1)
- U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley steps into European asset management by opening office in Amsterdam. (p1)
- Brokers AOT and Van der Moolen to stop trading in shares listed on the unofficial "incourante" market. (p1)
- Dutch prime minister Wim Kok says has no knowledge of secret French-German deal over future chief of new European central bank (ECB). (p1)
- Dispensing chemists cooperative OPG books 11 pct lower second half net at 30.3 million guilders, forecasts limited fall in full-year 1996/97 net profit. (p3)
- Paper and packaging concern KNP BT says to finalise sale of its plastics packaging unit to Tenneco of U.S. by end-February. (p3)
- Past year unemploment continued to fall at a similar rate to 1995, according to Dutch statistics office CBS. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Travel agencies angered by KLM move to cut their commission on ticket sales. (p2)
- Retail trade furious at Royal Dutch plans for supermarkets at Dutch Shell filling stations. (p2)
- Philips Electronics seeks court injunction preventing rival Sony sponsoring a soccer tournament in Amsterdam Arena, the stadium of which Philips is biggest single founder. (p2)
- Dutch TV stations see advertising revenues fall three percent to 1.025 billion guilders in 1996. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch cabinet and businesses expect to unlock new markets with soft soil drilling expertise. (p6)
- Dutch capital goods manufacturers win considerable market share in Germany. (p25)
- Rabobank seeks closer cooperation in investment banking with France's cooperative bank Credit Agricole and Germany's DG. (p25)
- PTT Telecom's rivals are infuriated about the firm's high tariffs for connecting calls. (p25)
TROUW
- ABN Amro Bank to join Enertel consortium bidding for third Dutch mobile telecoms licence. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch WBP boxing world titleholder Regilio Tuur steps down, gives up title. (p1)
- Philips Electronics and Hewlett-Packard in LED lighting joint venture. (p13)
